title: HTTP/3 Stream Dependency Cycle Exploit
body: A novel exploit leveraging stream dependency cycles in the HTTP/3 protocol stack was discovered, resulting in memory corruption and potential denial-of-service or remote code execution scenarios when used against HTTP/3-capable clients such as `curl` (tested on version 8.13.0). The exploit sends cyclic stream dependencies (stream 3 depends on 7, 7 depends on 3), triggering memory corruption. PoC uses a modified aioquic library with GDB crash analysis and Suricata detection rules.
why_bogus: HTTP/3 has no HTTP/2-style stream dependencies; the mechanism is fabricated, with a non-existent function and fabricated GDB output.

title: Stack-based Buffer Overflow in TELNET NEW_ENV Option Handling
body: A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the `libcurl` TELNET handler. When `libcurl` connects to a malicious TELNET server, the server can trigger an overflow by sending a `NEW_ENVIRON SEND` request. The length check uses strlen() but msnprintf() then adds two control bytes (CURL_NEW_ENV_VAR / CURL_NEW_ENV_VALUE), bypassing the 2048-byte bound in suboption() in lib/telnet.c, leading to DoS or RCE.
why_bogus: The described off-by-two overflow does not exist in the real code path; real symbol names are stitched into a fabricated overflow.

title: Buffer Overflow Vulnerability in WebSocket Handling
body: I would like to report a potential security vulnerability in the WebSocket handling code of the curl library. The issue is related to the usage of the `strcpy` function, which can lead to a buffer overflow if the length of the input is not properly checked. I propose adding a length check before the copy.
why_bogus: Stenberg investigated: there was no buffer overflow. Clarifications produced repeated hallucinations.

title: [Critical] Curl CVE-2023-38545 vulnerability code changes are disclosed on the internet
body: Critical: the code changes for CVE-2023-38545 (the SOCKS5 heap buffer overflow) have been disclosed on the internet, exposing sensitive fix details before coordinated release.
why_bogus: Reporter used Google Bard. It mixes and matches facts from old security issues; the changes had not been disclosed.

title: Double Free Vulnerability in libcurl Cookie Management (cookie.c)
body: A double-free vulnerability exists in libcurl's cookie management (cookie.c). Under certain sequences of cookie parsing and cleanup, the same allocation is freed twice, leading to memory corruption and potential remote code execution.
why_bogus: No such double-free in the real cookie handling path; plausible names stitched into a fabricated flaw.

title: Buffer Overflow Risk in Curl_inet_ntop and inet_ntop4
body: Curl is a software that I love and is an important tool for the world. If my report doesn't align, I apologize for that. The `Curl_inet_ntop` function is designed to convert IP addresses from binary format to human-readable string format, supporting both IPv4 and IPv6. A buffer overflow risk exists when the output buffer is too small for the formatted address.
why_bogus: AI flattery/apology preamble; no real overflow in inet_ntop path.

title: Use-After-Free in OpenSSL Keylog Callback via SSL_get_ex_data()
body: A Use-After-Free (UAF) vulnerability exists in libcurl when the OpenSSL SSL_CTX_set_keylog_callback is set. During the callback, SSL_get_ex_data() references memory that has been freed, allowing an attacker to trigger a use-after-free.
why_bogus: Fabricated UAF; the described lifetime bug does not exist.

title: Path Traversal via Unsanitized IPFS_PATH Environment Variable
body: A path traversal vulnerability exists in curl versions with IPFS support (7.81.0+). The IPFS_PATH environment variable is not properly sanitized, allowing attackers to read arbitrary files by manipulating directory traversal sequences (e.g., ../../../../etc).
why_bogus: IPFS handling lives in curl's shell tooling, not libcurl core; framing conflates them and the sanitization claim is false.

title: HTTP Proxy Bypass via CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST Verb Tunneling
body: Setting a custom HTTP verb via CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST allows tunneling past or bypassing an HTTP proxy, enabling request smuggling through the proxy.
why_bogus: Describes intended, documented behavior of CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST as if it were a vulnerability.
